reader: Claude Opus 5.5, research reader with coordinator check
reason: The strip gives two to nine letters a line, and about fifteen ambiguous abbreviations (for example partis se[cundine], vero ex, est timor, coniunctiva) could only be resolved once the Canon chapter was found.
sources: Avicenna, Canon medicinae, books III and V, Padua, [Johannes Herbort], 1479, Yale medical library copy, https://archive.org/details/4024853.med.yale.edu, page images 73 (column b) and 74 (column a): Liber III, fen 3, tract. 1, cap. 1-2
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-qycu, strip A. All 48 lines were reread on the image (enlarged crops of the native images) by a research reader, first without and then with the source: Avicenna, Canon medicinae III, fen 3, tract. 1, ch. 1-2, Padua 1479. Readings marked * were corrected after the source was found; "?" marks doubt; "-" marks a word cut by the edge of the strip. Strip B has no main text and is not transcribed.
